ops.text: 9A. Indemnification. (a) HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Site, the services, software, tools, systems or other materials provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right (other than to the extent arising from Content or Marks provided by the Company); (ii) HDI's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Confidential Information or customer data caused by HDI; or (iv) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct. (b) The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right or out of the Company's breach of applicable law. (c) The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnity is sought; the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim, provided that it shall not enter into any settlement that imposes any liability or obligation on, or requires any admission by, the indemnified Party without the indemnified Party's prior written consent; and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 9A adding HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality breach, gross negligence/willful misconduct), a narrow reciprocal Company indemnity for Content and Marks it supplies, and standard indemnity procedure.

rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification, hold-harmless or defense provision anywhere: searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "infringe" return no indemnity language, and the document moves directly from the mutual warranties in Section 9 (p0055–p0058) to General Provisions in Section 10 (p0059 onward). HDI therefore owes no indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from the Site or hosted services, nor for its own breach of law, breach of the confidentiality/customer-data obligations in Section 8, or gross negligence or willful misconduct — which is walk-away territory under the rule (no vendor IP indemnity at all). We have inserted a new Section 9A providing HDI's indemnity per the model language, with our reciprocal indemnity narrowed to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law, plus standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics.

ops.text: 9A. Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), and neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligation to pay amounts due under Section 3 shall not be subject to the foregoing limitation.

rationale: The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, damages exclusion or "aggregate liability" language anywhere: searches for "liability", "liable", "damages", "consequential" and "indemnif" return only the No Joint Venture provision (p0061-p0062), and the Warranties section (p0055-p0058) and General Provisions (p0059-p0070) are silent on liability. quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: Section 6.1 imposes an exclusivity/sole-channel covenant on us as customer: we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or for "products substantially similar" to them, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online. This fails the fallback on two material terms. (1) Duration: it runs "during the term of this Agreement", and the term under Section 4.1 auto-renews for successive one-year periods, so the lock-up is open-ended rather than capped at 12 months; our only exit is 90 days' notice, which triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a) (Net Sales for the preceding 12 months less $800,000, halved). (2) No performance-based release: the Agreement contains no service levels and no termination-for-breach right; the only penalty-free exit (Section 1.6) is a one-off launch-date failure at the outset, after which exclusivity continues regardless of HDI's performance. That is effectively exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance exit. Scope is also broader than a defined product category, extending to competitor-type goods (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and similar). The Section 6.2 closeout-merchandise carve-out and HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and we leave untouched) mitigate but do not cure this. Given HDI's build-and-host investment and the reciprocal covenant, we propose the fallback rather than deletion: narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months from the Effective Date, and release automatically (with no Termination Payment) on HDI's failure to meet its Article 1 delivery and performance obligations.

quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: Section 6 ("Exclusivity") does bind us, but it sits at the playbook fallback rather than in deviation territory. The restriction (i) applies "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail at all (the two-year tail in Section 6.3 runs against HDI, which is to our benefit and is not flagged), and the term is terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (Section 4.1); (ii) is confined to a named product line and named competitors — participating in "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled), rather than an undefined "any competing business"; and (iii) carries carve-outs: Section 6.2 preserves our right to run a closeout-merchandise site, and the definition of "Deerskin Products" in Section 1.1 excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog, so other channels, catalogs and product lines are untouched. It does not restrict what we may buy or build generally. Short of the preferred position (no restriction at all) we note two sub-elements for the negotiation record but do not redline them: the elastic reach of "products substantially similar" / "companies similar to", and the absence of an express carve-out for internal development and acquisitions. quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
rationale: Section 10.5 selects the laws of the State of New York, which is the playbook's preferred governing law, and expressly disapplies conflict-of-laws principles. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "arbitration" and any dispute-forum language return nothing), so disputes default to the courts rather than a foreign arbitral seat, and no foreign exclusive venue is imposed. The only shortfall against the preferred position is the absence of an express exclusive-venue designation for the state and federal courts in New York County; that is a missing mechanic rather than a material failure, since silence leaves ordinary court jurisdiction available and does not disadvantage us. We would add the New York County exclusive-venue sentence if the document is being amended for other reasons, but it does not warrant a redline on its own.

rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic running in either direction. The economics in §3 (Fees; Payment) are a fixed revenue-share of Net Sales with no obligation on the Company to match third-party terms, to extend to HDI any better pricing or terms granted to others, or to match competing offers; searches for "favorable"/"most favoured"/"best"/"price"/"rates"/"terms and conditions" returned nothing of that character. The only restriction on the Company is the §6.1 exclusivity/non-compete covenant (limited by §6.2), which is a scope restriction rather than an MFN and is addressed under the exclusivity rule, so it is not flagged here. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdening the Customer — so no redline is proposed. Noted only for the record: there is also no MFN in our favour, which is welcome but not required by this rule.
sectionRef: § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
rationale: The fee structure meets the preferred position: the Company owes HDI only a 30% share of actual Net Sales generated on the Site, and only on sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold, so all amounts are purely usage-based. The Company also has a clean annual exit on 90 days' notice under Section 4.1. Two adjacent points are noted for completeness but are not MINCOMMIT deviations and are better addressed under the termination-fee and exclusivity rules: the Section 4.2 Termination Payment (12-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved) is an exit fee rather than a volume commitment or shortfall penalty, and the Section 6.1 exclusivity restricts competing online channels rather than capping or committing Company volumes.

Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including migration of the Site and the URL, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information and customer and order data relating to the Site or the Deerskin Products, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, information and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing.

rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; it contains no exit obligations. Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement supplies them: Section 1.5 export files apply only during operation, the confidentiality provisions (8.1-8.3) impose no return or destruction duty, and the survival clause (10.7) omits Sections 4, 5 and 8 entirely. HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer/order data, so the Agreement falls below even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus data export within 30 days) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. Inserted a new Section 4.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and customer/order data in a machine-readable format within 30 days of the Termination Date, and certified deletion thereafter.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains only mutual corporate authority warranties, so HDI gives no warranty at all for the development and hosting work it performs. We have added our standard performance and conformance warranty (professional and workmanlike, conformance to the specifications approved under Section 5.2, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a re-performance, repair/replace or refund remedy. We can discuss shortening the conformance period to ninety (90) days if HDI prefers.

ops.text: (c) HDI represents and warrants to the Company that (1) the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance, management and hosting of the Site (collectively, the "Services") will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (2) for a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, the Site will conform in all material respects to the specifications and documentation approved by the Company pursuant to Section 5.2; (3) HDI will perform the Services in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations; and (4) the Site and any software or code delivered or used by HDI in connection with the Services will be free of any virus, worm, disabling device or other malicious code. The Company's remedy for breach of this Section 9(c) shall be, at HDI's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Services or Site, or a refund of the fees paid or payable to HDI in respect of the non-conforming Services or Site, and if HDI fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days of written notice from the Company, the Company may terminate this Agreement without penalty and without any Termination Payment.

proposal.summary: Insert HDI performance, conformance, legal-compliance and no-malicious-code warranties with a real remedy into Section 9.

rationale: Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate-existence/authority representations (p0056-p0057) and a Globix Agreement acknowledgement (p0058). Nowhere in the Agreement does HDI warrant the quality or conformance of the development or hosting work it performs: there is no professional/workmanlike standard, no conformance-to-specification warranty or period, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy (searches for "warrant", "workmanlike", "industry standard", "virus", "AS IS" and "MERCHANTABILITY" return nothing else). Section 1.6 gives only a go-live termination right, which is not a performance warranty. Because there is no express performance warranty at all, the clause fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies); the only mitigating fact is that there is also no disclaimer, so this is not full walk-away "AS IS" territory. Per the detection guidance, a missing express warranty is a deviation, and we have inserted a new Section 9(c) with the preferred warranty set and a real remedy (re-performance, repair/replacement or refund, plus termination without Termination Payment on failure to cure), noting that a 90-day conformance period is an acceptable fallback.

ops.text: 10.9 Insurance. HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) for so long as HDI hosts the Site or has access to Confidential Information or user data of the Company, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. HDI shall provide the Company with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 10.9 (Insurance) requiring HDI to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation coverage with certificates on request.

quote: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere: searches for "insur" and "indemnif" return no hits, and a full read of the General Provisions (Section 10, p0059-p0070) and the operative sections shows notices, no joint venture, assignment, waiver, governing law, severability, survival, entire agreement and headings, but no insurance requirement. HDI is a services/hosting vendor that designs, hosts and maintains the Site on its own server (p0005, p0007) and expressly "may have access to or be exposed to... Content, user information, data" and Confidential Information of the Company (p0048), so it both processes our data and performs services for us. Under the rule this is walk-away territory (no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data), so we insert the preferred package as new Section 10.9 immediately after the final General Provisions paragraph: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M while HDI hosts the Site or holds Confidential Information or user data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. Existing Section 10.7 survival (p0068) already carries Section 10 for two years post-termination, so the one-year tail is consistent. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment as a landing zone.
